name: login
title: Login
description: The sign-in surface, rendered. BDS-041: it never performs authentication. No network call, no cookie, no token, no identity provider; it collects what the player typed and reports it, and the host sends the code, checks the password and decides who this is. Three ways in, in the order the design draws them: an identifier field with the primary action, then the providers under a divider, then the way past all of it. The escape is part of the surface rather than something a host remembers to add, because a player who will not sign in is a player who leaves. Refusal is the host's word and arrives as `invalid` plus a reason; `busy` is host-declared and takes every control out of reach while the host has not answered.
docs: Pass `onSubmit` and read the identifier out of the values it hands you; send your own code or check your own password from there. Pass `providers` as `[{ id, label, icon }]` and `onProvider` to open each one yourself, drawing any mark as inline SVG on `currentColor`. Pass `onGuest` when your game has somewhere for a player to go without an account, and leave it out when it does not. While your own call is in flight set `busy`; when it comes back refused, set `invalid` and pass your own sentence as `reason`. Find the escape with `[data-gs-part="guest"]` and each provider with `[data-gs-part="provider"]`.
